message: EBS Default Encryption is not activated.
status_detail: EBS Default Encryption is not activated.

finding_info.desc: **EBS** uses `encryption by default` at the account and region level, ensuring new volumes, snapshots, and AMI-backed volumes are automatically encrypted with a chosen **KMS key**
finding_info.title: EBS default encryption is enabled
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark
Effects/Data Exposure

remediation.desc: Enable `EBS encryption by default` in every region and select a **customer-managed KMS key**. Apply **least privilege** to key use, rotate keys, and monitor access. Enforce encrypted volume creation with organizational guardrails and secure templates as **defense in depth**.

risk_details: Without `encryption by default`, data on new **EBS volumes** and **snapshots** may be stored in plaintext. A compromised account or mis-shared snapshot can expose disk contents, enabling data exfiltration, offline analysis, and loss of **confidentiality**.

message: Network ACL acl-default has every port open to the Internet.
status_detail: Network ACL acl-default has every port open to the Internet.

analytic.name: Network ACL does not allow ingress from 0.0.0.0/0 to any port

finding_info.desc: **VPC network ACLs** with **inbound entries** that permit traffic from `0.0.0.0/0` to any port (any protocol) are identified at the subnet boundary.
finding_info.title: Network ACL does not allow ingress from 0.0.0.0/0 to any port
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices/Network Reachability
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark
TTPs/Initial Access/Unauthorized Access
Effects/Data Exposure

remediation.desc: Adopt a **deny-by-default** NACL posture: block `0.0.0.0/0` and allow only required ports from trusted CIDRs. Apply **least privilege** using security groups for fine-grained access, with NACLs as coarse stateless filters. Review and prune rules regularly, and employ **defense in depth** with monitoring and alerting.

risk_details: Allowing Internet-wide ingress at the subnet layer enables broad port scanning and unsolicited connections. Attackers can probe and exploit exposed services, risking data disclosure and tampering (confidentiality, integrity) and causing outages via floods or brute-force (availability). Any security group lapse then lacks a compensating control.

message: Network ACL acl-default has SSH port 22 open to the Internet.
status_detail: Network ACL acl-default has SSH port 22 open to the Internet.

analytic.name: Network ACL does not allow ingress from the Internet to TCP port 22 (SSH)

finding_info.desc: **VPC network ACLs** are evaluated for inbound rules that permit `0.0.0.0/0` to access **SSH** on `TCP 22` at the subnet boundary.
finding_info.title: Network ACL does not allow ingress from the Internet to TCP port 22 (SSH)
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices/Network Reachability
TTPs/Initial Access

remediation.desc:
Apply **least privilege** at the subnet layer:
- Do not allow `0.0.0.0/0` to `TCP 22`
- Restrict SSH to trusted sources, or avoid direct SSH via **Session Manager** or a bastion behind **VPN**

Pair tight **security groups** with periodic rule reviews and change control to maintain **defense in depth**.

risk_details:
An ACL allowing Internet-wide SSH erodes **defense in depth**. Systems reachable on `TCP 22` face **brute-force**, credential stuffing, reconnaissance, and SSH exploit attempts.

Changes to routes or security groups can create direct exposure, enabling unauthorized access and **lateral movement**, undermining **confidentiality** and **integrity**.

message: Network ACL acl-default has Microsoft RDP port 3389 open to the Internet.
status_detail: Network ACL acl-default has Microsoft RDP port 3389 open to the Internet.

analytic.name: Network ACL does not allow ingress from the Internet to TCP port 3389 (RDP)

finding_info.desc:
**VPC network ACLs** with inbound rules allowing **RDP** on `TCP 3389` from `0.0.0.0/0` are identified.

Assessment focuses on subnet-level ACL entries that permit this traffic.
finding_info.title: Network ACL does not allow ingress from the Internet to TCP port 3389 (RDP)
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices/Network Reachability
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark
TTPs/Initial Access

remediation.desc:
Enforce **least privilege**: do not allow `TCP 3389` from `0.0.0.0/0` in network ACLs.

- Restrict RDP to specific admin IP ranges
- Prefer **bastion hosts** or **Session Manager** over direct RDP
- Use private subnets and layer controls for **defense in depth**

risk_details: Internet-exposed **RDP** enables **password spraying**, brute force, and exploitation of RDP flaws to gain remote control. Allowing it at the subnet layer weakens **defense in depth**-a misconfigured security group or route can expose instances-leading to data exfiltration, privilege escalation, and ransomware, impacting confidentiality and integrity.

message: Cluster endpoint private access is not enabled for EKS cluster nr-eks.
status_detail: Cluster endpoint private access is not enabled for EKS cluster nr-eks.

unmapped.notes: Enabling private nodes restricts outbound access to the public internet. If outbound internet access is required, Cloud NAT or a NAT gateway can be used.

analytic.name: EKS cluster has private endpoint access enabled

finding_info.desc:
**Amazon EKS cluster** has **private endpoint access** enabled for the **Kubernetes API server**, allowing control plane traffic to use a VPC-resolved private endpoint.

The check evaluates the cluster's `endpointPrivateAccess` setting.
finding_info.title: EKS cluster has private endpoint access enabled
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices/Network Reachability
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices
TTPs/Initial Access/Unauthorized Access
api
audit
authenticator
controllerManager
scheduler

remediation.desc:
Enable **private endpoint access** and disable or tightly restrict the public endpoint.

Require administration from private networks, enforce **least privilege** with IAM/RBAC, and apply **defense in depth** via segmentation and logging. *If external access is needed*, allow only specific CIDRs and monitor API activity.

risk_details: Without **private endpoint access**, the API server is exposed on the public internet. This expands attack surface and weakens **confidentiality** and **integrity**: stolen creds or mis-scoped CIDRs can enable unauthorized API calls, secret reads, pod deployments, and config changes. **Availability** also depends on internet egress, increasing failure modes.

message: S3 Bucket nr-plain has bucket ACLs enabled.
status_detail: S3 Bucket nr-plain has bucket ACLs enabled.

analytic.name: S3 bucket has bucket ACLs disabled

finding_info.desc: **Amazon S3 buckets** are evaluated for **Object Ownership** set to `BucketOwnerEnforced`, which disables bucket and object ACLs. Buckets using any other ownership setting indicate that ACLs remain enabled.
finding_info.title: S3 bucket has bucket ACLs disabled
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark

remediation.desc: Disable ACLs by setting **Object Ownership** to `BucketOwnerEnforced` and manage access with **IAM** and **bucket policies** under **least privilege**. Centralize authorization, review policies regularly, and use organizational guardrails to prevent re-enabling ACLs. *Migrate ACL-based grants into policies before the change.*

risk_details:
With **ACLs enabled**, access can bypass centralized policy controls, impacting confidentiality and integrity.
- Unintended public or cross-account reads/writes
- Object-writer ownership blocking bucket-owner governance
- Per-object grants hinder auditing, enabling data exfiltration or tampering

message: S3 Bucket nr-plain does not have a bucket policy, thus it allows HTTP requests.
status_detail: S3 Bucket nr-plain does not have a bucket policy, thus it allows HTTP requests.

analytic.name: S3 bucket policy denies requests over insecure transport

finding_info.desc:
**Amazon S3 buckets** are evaluated for a bucket policy that enforces **secure transport** by denying requests when `aws:SecureTransport` is `false`.

Buckets without this explicit denial, or without a policy, are treated as allowing access over insecure transport.
finding_info.title: S3 bucket policy denies requests over insecure transport
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices/Network Reachability
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark

remediation.desc:
Enforce **HTTPS-only** access with a bucket policy that denies requests when `aws:SecureTransport=false`.

Prefer **private access** (VPC endpoints or CloudFront with TLS), avoid S3 website endpoints, apply **least privilege**, use short-lived HTTPS **pre-signed URLs**, and monitor logs for insecure access attempts.

risk_details: HTTP access exposes object data and auth details to **eavesdropping** and **man-in-the-middle** attacks. Captured **pre-signed URLs** can be replayed to exfiltrate data. Traffic can be intercepted or altered, undermining **confidentiality** and **integrity** of S3 content.

message: S3 Bucket nr-plain has server access logging disabled.
status_detail: S3 Bucket nr-plain has server access logging disabled.

analytic.name: S3 bucket has server access logging enabled

finding_info.desc: **Amazon S3 buckets** are evaluated for **server access logging** configured to record access requests and deliver logs to a designated destination bucket.
finding_info.title: S3 bucket has server access logging enabled
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark

remediation.desc: Enable **server access logging** and send logs to a dedicated log bucket with least privilege, retention, and monitoring. Complement with **CloudTrail data events** for object-level visibility. Apply **defense in depth** by centralizing logs and protecting them from tampering.

risk_details: Without access logs, object reads, writes, and deletions may go untracked, hindering detection of unauthorized access and data exfiltration. This degrades forensic visibility, delays incident response, and weakens evidence integrity, impacting confidentiality and integrity.
